#### 1. otospondylomegaepiphyseal dysplasia, autosomal recessive  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.791)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:2187)

**Proposed mechanism:** COL11A2 (HGNC:2187) —DISRUPTS→ Type XI collagen synthesis and extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Type XI collagen synthesis and extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0005974); Type XI collagen synthesis and extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Hearing impairment (HP:0000365); Type XI collagen synthesis and extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Myopia (HP:0000540); Type XI collagen synthesis and extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Cleft palate (HP:0000175); Type XI collagen synthesis and extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004322); Type XI collagen synthesis and extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Epiphyseal dysplasia (HP:0002717). Loss-of-function mutations in COL11A2 disrupt the synthesis of functional Type XI collagen, a critical component of cartilage and connective tissues. This disruption leads to a spectrum of skeletal abnormalities, including epiphyseal dysplasia and short stature, as well as other connective tissue defects manifesting as hearing impairment, myopia, and cleft palate.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in COL11A2 that are exclusively associated with one disease phenotype and not the other, or identification of distinct pathogenic variants in other genes that fully explain the phenotype of one disease while COL11A2 variants explain the other. _(variant: Any pathogenic variant in HGNC:2187 with a minor allele frequency > 0.01 in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in COL11A2 provides a unified target for therapeutic strategies aimed at improving collagen synthesis or function, potentially benefiting patients with both conditions.

This dysfunction in collagen formation underlies the shared skeletal, ocular, and auditory phenotypes observed in both Osteogenesis imperfecta type V and otospondylomegaepiphyseal dysplasia, autosomal dominant.

**How to falsify it:** The presence of pathogenic variants in COL11A2 with a clear loss-of-function or haploinsufficiency mechanism in patients with both MONDO:0013795 and MONDO:0008490 would support this hypothesis. **Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in COL11A2 could enable the development of targeted therapies for both Osteogenesis imperfecta type V and otospondylomegaepiphyseal dysplasia, autosomal dominant, potentially by modulating collagen production or stability.
